what: Raja Himmat Gir Goshain commanded about 1,000 Naga cavalry under Shuja-ud-daula; received pargana Amethi in jagir; built the market (Goshainganj); fort remains; later retired to a small jagir near Hardwar
quote: old fort of Raja Himmat Gir Goshain, who commanded a force of some 1,000 Naga cavalry in the time of Shuja-ud-danla, He received the pargana of Amethi in jagir

what: Himmat Gir's jagir of Amethi pargana (later Goshainganj pargana, name derived from his market)
quote: He received the pargana of Amethi in jagir and built the market here which subsequently, in 1857, gave its name to the pargana.

what: Mahant Harcharan Das, a Nanakshahi faqir, successor of Mahant Gurnarain Das who founded the estate under the Nawabi; owns estates in Gonda, Hardoi, Kheri and 4 villages Sarai Pemraj (Rs 2,478) in Lucknow; also Reari (Malihabad) and an estate in pargana Mohanlalganj
quote: He is a Nanakshahi faqir and the successor of Mahant Gurnarain Das, who founded the estate during the later days of tho Nawabi rule.

what: Of 34 taluqdars holding land in the district, one is a Nanakshahi faqir (the Mahant)
quote: Of these, 14 are Musalmans, 11 Rajputs, three each Brahmans and Kayasths, two Khattris and one a Nanakshahi faqfr.

what: Tradition: devotees and anchorites founded towns; Juggaur attributed to Jagdeo Jogi (legendary)
quote: Juggaur, attributed to Jagdeo Jogi; they are said to haye received the land in jagir from Janamejaya

what: Jogia Mela: great August fair in Qaisarbagh in Wajid Ali Shah's time; Wajid Ali sat dressed as a faqir (court entertainment, not an ascetic gathering)
quote: a great fair used to be held here, known as the Jogia Mela, to which the whole town was admitted.

what: Faqirs (Muslim) number over 2,500; no Hindu ascetic orders (Gosain, Bairagi etc.) counted in text
quote: Quassabs, Kunjras, Faqirs, Gaddis, Darzis, Nais and Bhangis all number over 2,500
